title: Attempts and lessons
prompt: This program counts the rows of the `attempts` and `lessons` tables and compares their columns. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
hints: There are three `print` calls, so there are three lines.
`count()` counts the rows of a table; the header with the column names isn't a row.
`columns` is a list of names. Count the columns of each table, then subtract.
explanation: `count()` gives back the number of rows as a plain Python number: 13 attempts and 8 lessons. `attempts` has 8 columns and `lessons` has 5, and because `columns` is an ordinary list, `len` and subtraction work on it like on any list.
